statement: A running track has two straight sides, each $80$ meters long, joined at each end by a semicircle. The straight sides are $40$ meters apart, so each semicircle has a diameter of $40$ meters. What is the total distance, in meters, once around the track?

choices.misconception: I used 40 meters as the radius of each semicircle, so each curved end was 40 pi and the two ends together were 80 pi.
I added the two 40 meter diameters to the perimeter as if they were part of the track, even though the semicircles replace them.
I added only one semicircle, which is 20 pi, and forgot that the track has a curved end at each side.

hints: The distance around is the two straight sides plus the two curved ends.
The two semicircles have the same diameter, so together they make one full circle of diameter $40$.
A circle of diameter $40$ has circumference $40\pi$. Add the two $80$ meter sides.

solutions.reliable: The straight parts give $2 \cdot 80 = 160$ meters. Each curved end is a semicircle of diameter $40$, so its length is $\frac{1}{2} \pi (40) = 20\pi$. The two ends give $40\pi$. The total is $160 + 40\pi$ meters, about $285.7$ meters.
solutions.elegant: Push the two semicircles together and they form one full circle of diameter $40$, with circumference $40\pi$. Add the straightaways: $160 + 40\pi$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
